name: Hearthbloom Basin
core_rationale: Formed inside Sola the Hearth-Weaver's fallen ceramic shield (scar-kiln-basin), serving as the warm, low-hazard Level 1 to 15 starter continent where Star-Kindled Sprouts first awaken.

parent_world_history_causes.causal_summary: Sola's eternal ember-heart beneath the clay soil keeps the basin at perpetual spring and powers the town hearths.

climate_profile.macro_biome: Sun-baked terracotta terraces, short clover meadows, and warm thermal creeks
weather_phenomena: Gentle ember-pollen drift across warm afternoon breezes
climate_profile.skybox_palette: Golden-hour apricot sky with soft cumulus clouds

civilization_style.architecture_motif: Glazed teapot-domed cottages, brick archways, and waterwheel bakeries
civilization_style.character_scale_adaptation: All cottages use 2.0 by 1.5 meter keyhole doorways, 0.14 meter step risers, 0.58 meter bakery counters, and clover grass capped at 0.25 meters so 1.05 meter Sprouts have unobstructed sightlines.

travel_links.unlock_rationale: Repaired upon completing the Level 15 Hearthbloom main story chapter.
Opened after igniting the Crown Beacon Citadel star-lighthouse in The Zenith Crown on Continent 03.

causal_continuity.evidence: Directly inherits god-sola-hearth-weaver and scar-kiln-basin from world-history-cradle-of-embers and hosts the bound Starter Town town-lantern-hollow.

fantasy_and_wonder.evidence: Glazed teapot-domed villages and warm terracotta caldera terraces powered by a slumbering Goddess's ceramic shield.

character_scale_consistency.evidence: Enforces 2.0x1.5m keyhole doorways, 0.14m stair risers, 0.58m shop counters, and 0.25m clover grass for 0.90 to 1.20 meter characters.

spatial_and_ecological_consistency.evidence: Organizes ten Canon Districts plus Cardamom-Kiln Caldera (Mystery) on Continent 01.

intentional_mystery_discipline.evidence: Seeds Cardamom-Kiln Caldera in Mystery status while preserving leaf Mystery nodes behind fog_of_lore gates.

mystery_hook.in_world_rumor: Bathhouse keepers in Ginger-Bathhouse Haven say the eastern Cardamom-Kiln Caldera simmers with spiced porcelain glaze-springs that glow amber beneath the evening mist.
mystery_hook.visual_silhouette: Dome-shaped cardamom drying kilns and terraced porcelain glaze-basins rising beyond the northern rim above Ginger-Steam Terraces.
mystery_hook.unanswered_question: Which Primordial Kiln-Artisan carved the central spice-glaze crucible of Cardamom-Kiln Caldera?
mystery_hook.discovery_trigger_hint: Ten Districts on Continent 01 are Canon while Cardamom-Kiln Caldera awaits exploration along the north-western geothermal rim.

district_links.transition: The clover gives way to pale clay and the creek warms slightly; the road climbs a little as white domes appear above the rim.
Brick steps climb from warm clover into cooler, drier air, and the creek sounds drop away behind you as kiln updrafts begin.
A bridge crosses the Glaze River just below where the meadow creeks join it, and the road climbs west into steam from the mineral pools.
The trail leaves the orchard east of Lantern Hollow and enters damp shade as the first banyan roots cross the path.
The terraces end at the aqueduct spill, and the ford leads down into wet warm channels and fog.
A pass over the dry ridge, with the orchards behind you and the trench ahead showing grey ash slopes.
A firebrick tunnel leads from the dry trench into a wetter place where the walls turn from ash to resin and roots.
The road climbs from damp root shade into dry stone, and the air becomes cooler and windier.
An old stair climbs from the lake rim to the kiln terraces, and the white clay turns to dry stone as the air cools.
A footbridge crosses a warm creek on a rough path, and steam from the Ginger terraces appears in the trees to the south-west.
The road leaves the steam, climbs through trees to a breezier bluff, and cinnamon bark windbreaks replace the ginger fields.
Steps follow the run-off from the travertine pools beside the Glaze River down to the delta, ending in fog and braided channels.
The pass climbs from the forest edge through old trees onto bare ground and strong dry wind, and the first ceramic pipes can be heard well before the arches are seen.
A trail climbs north from the bluff through old forest beside the Glaze River into wetter air, ending at the caldera rim with mist below.
An old tunnel runs from the wet caldera under the ridge, and you leave the mist for bare, dry wind at the far end, above a deep forested valley.
An old bridge crosses a gap between the caldera and the kiln terraces; the mist stays behind you and the stone gets drier.
The road leaves the clover and runs south-east, narrowing into the choke point guarded by Daro Post before it opens onto the grey ash slopes of the trench.
The trail leaves the forest edge of the bluff, drops east-north-east through open woodland and ends at the pale clay rim of the Porcelain Cradle.

transport_links.note: Scheduled freight caravan or ancient transit connection via Kilnwatch, never an ordinary adjacent map edge (reply 4.1: Ondo-Linde keep as transport).
Scheduled commercial transport with intermediate stops. The reply allows a boat only if the Glaze River course permits it; the river does not pass the Wind-Chime ridge, so this is a caravan.

Lead override of the reply (which proposed a protected highland trail): an underground route along the bellows ducts, since the Ash-Bellows district text says its air is ducted under the basin to Kilnfire. Not a surface trail.
